title: Meeting backbone — warehouse inventory scoping
description: Video 1 is the backbone of the meeting section because it contains the “why are we even building this?” story. Video 2 refines requirements, constraints, and scope. Source ranges are pulled from WhisperX transcripts; tighten start/end further toward each target_length as needed.

videos.label: Video 1 — 2026-08-05 14-52-57
videos.description: Most of the story/problem definition lives here. Expect roughly 5–6 minutes to survive the edit.

timestamps.title: Series/project hook — taking an idea to production in under 24 hours
timestamps.description: Establishes the series premise and deadline challenge.

timestamps.title: Why the project matters personally — Aniah is anxious, stepped away from business, wants to get back into it
timestamps.description: Personal stakes before the business problem.

timestamps.title: The core business problem — inquiry → availability check → quote → mistakes → two-hour trip for glasses
timestamps.transcript_cue: Inquiry / quote / warehouse mismatch / two-hour drive for glasses
timestamps.description: Strongest stakeholder clip. Source range is longer than target — trim middle if needed.

timestamps.title: You restate the problem + propose the first solution
timestamps.transcript_cue: “Desired result is a client can click buy…” → warehouse grid/locations/app
timestamps.description: Problem restatement into first proposed solution shape.

timestamps.title: Second problem emerges: “I don't even know what I have”
timestamps.description: Catalog/inventory blindness as a second problem.

timestamps.title: You recognize there are actually two flows and narrow this project
timestamps.description: Narrows scope to WMS/cataloging for this project.

timestamps.title: Usability requirement — “make it dummy proof,” very streamlined
timestamps.description: Important UX requirement for the cataloging app.

videos.label: Video 2 — 2026-08-05 15-18-39
videos.description: Requirements refinement, correcting assumptions, constraints, and scope creep. Aim for about 3–4 minutes.

timestamps.title: Mobile vs. desktop assumption gets challenged
timestamps.transcript_cue: You propose interfaces → Aniah says she pulls inventory from her phone
timestamps.description: Assumption correction that reshapes mobile vs web roles.

timestamps.title: Mobile becomes streamlined; web becomes detailed management
timestamps.transcript_cue: Photo/title/quantity on mobile; descriptions/pricing/etc. later on web
timestamps.description: Split of responsibilities between app and web.

timestamps.title: Employee requirement creates roles + pick/return workflow
timestamps.transcript_cue: Broken/missing glasses → employees only need pick/return access
timestamps.description: Introduces Admin vs Staff roles and pick/return.

timestamps.title: Project constraints — 24 hours, $0, quality can come later
Acceptance criteria recap
timestamps.transcript_cue: Admin, Staff, mobile, web, detailed records
timestamps.description: Acceptance criteria snapshot before scope creep.

timestamps.title: Scope-creep montage — calendar
timestamps.description: Montage beat 1/3. Compress with the next two for humor/education — do not keep the whole discussion.

timestamps.title: Scope-creep montage — overbooking
timestamps.transcript_cue: “Basically, you want to be able to overbook items.”

timestamps.title: Scope-creep montage — substitutions
timestamps.description: Montage beat 3/3. Consider disabling some beats if the montage runs long.

timestamps.title: Meeting conclusion
timestamps.transcript_cue: “This gives me a really good starting point…” → app/web/barcodes/warehouse diagram
